title: I stopped scrubbing through long YouTube videos after tapping this hidden Gemini button
excerpt: I'll never watch long tutorials the old way again
content_html:
Published Aug 5, 2026, 5:15 PM EDT

I cover Android with a focus on productivity, automation, and Google’s ecosystem, including Gemini and everyday apps. With a background in engineering and software development, I tend to go beyond surface-level tips and focus on how features fit into real workflows.
Before joining AP, I wrote for tech publications such as Gizbot in 2023 and iJunkie (formerly known as iPhoneHacks) from 2021 to 2022.

Watching videos on YouTube usually means sitting through the entire clip. If a section goes by too quickly or something isn’t clear, the only option is to rewind, scan the comments, or look up the topic somewhere else.

At some point, I noticed the Ask button, powered by Google Gemini, while watching videos on my phone. I ignored it at first, assuming it only generated a generic summary of the video.

But after finally trying it, I realized it wasn’t what I expected. Instead of passively watching on my phone, I can ask questions about a video as it plays.

Gemini summarizes what the video is about, explains confusing parts, or extracts key takeaways without jumping between apps.

Here’s how it completely changed my watching experience.

How to access the Ask feature

Press a button and ask your questions

You can access the Ask feature while watching a video on the YouTube mobile app (Android or iPhone) or on the YouTube website on desktop.

When available, the Ask button is located below the video player, typically between the Share and Download buttons. Tapping it opens a chat panel where you can type questions about the video or choose suggested prompts, like Summarize the video.

If you don’t see the Ask button below a video, click the three-dot menu icon next to the video controls.

The Ask feature is available for users in countries such as the United States, Canada, New Zealand, Japan, India, and others, with plans to expand to additional countries.

Because the rollout is ongoing, some users may see the Ask button while others don’t, even if they use the same device or app version. Google is expected to expand access as the feature becomes more stable.

When I realized the Ask feature was available inside YouTube, I experimented with it while watching videos. It didn’t take long to notice a few situations where it became genuinely useful.

Catching up when I lose track of a video

It was time to give the rewind button a rest

The Ask feature has been helpful when I lose track of what’s happening in a video. It happens more often than I’d like to admit, especially with longer videos or when I’m multitasking.

The only way to recover is to rewind the video and figure out where things started making sense. That can be frustrating if the explanation was long or if the creator moved quickly through several points.

Using the Ask button on YouTube changes that. Instead of scrubbing through the timeline, I can ask, “What are the main points of this section?”

Gemini provides a summary of the video’s content with timestamps, allowing me to stay focused without having to rewatch the entire thing.

Deciding whether a long video is worth watching

A quick summary gives me the gist of the story

Another situation where the Ask feature has been useful is when I am deciding whether a long video is worth my time.

YouTube is full of videos that run for 15, 20, or 40 minutes, and it is not always obvious from the title or thumbnail whether the content will be helpful.

Normally, I would skip through parts of the video or read the description to get a rough idea of what it covers. But that does not always give a clear picture.

Using the Ask button on YouTube makes this easier. I can ask it to summarize the video or highlight the main points before I commit to watching the whole thing.

If the summary sounds interesting, I will keep watching. If not, I can move on to something else without spending several minutes trying to figure that out myself.

Turning tutorials into step-by-step instructions

Simple steps make it easier to learn new topics

Many YouTube tutorials walk through several steps in a row, and it’s easy to miss something important if the creator moves quickly.

I would pause the video repeatedly or rewind to double-check what the next step was. That works, but it can turn a simple tutorial into a lot of back-and-forth scrubbing through the timeline.

Using the Ask button, I can request Google Gemini to simplify the instructions into clear steps.

For example, I might ask it to “list the steps shown in this video” or “turn this tutorial into step-by-step instructions.” Gemini summarizes the process into a simple list that’s easier to follow.

Copy the instructions and paste them into a document to save or reference them later.

Finding the part of the video that matters

I love skipping to the good parts

One of the most frustrating things about YouTube is searching within a video.

Even when creators add chapters, the exact moment you’re looking for isn’t always obvious. Gemini helps narrow things down much faster.

I can ask questions like, “When does the creator talk about battery life?” or “Where do they explain the camera settings?”

Gemini points me to the relevant portion of the video, making it easier to jump to the information I want.

A more interactive way to watch YouTube

After using YouTube’s Ask button a few times, I discovered that it is much more useful when used with a video rather than as a simple summary tool.

Asking questions, clarifying confusing parts, or quickly understanding the main points makes watching videos far more interactive.

I still watch YouTube the same way most of the time, especially when I’m enjoying a creator’s storytelling or watching something purely for entertainment.

However, when I’m trying to learn something, follow a tutorial, or understand a long video, the Ask feature has become something I now rely on regularly.

content_html_zh:
发布于 2026 年 8 月 5 日下午 5:15（美国东部时间）

我介绍 Android 时，重点关注生产力、自动化和 Google 生态系统，包括 Gemini 和日常应用程序。 凭借工程和软件开发的背景，我倾向于超越表面技巧，而专注于功能如何融入实际工作流程。 在加入 AP 之前，我曾为科技出版物撰写文章，例如 2023 年为 Gizbot 撰写文章，2021 年至 2022 年为 iJunkie（以前称为 iPhoneHacks）撰写文章。

在 YouTube 上观看视频通常需要观看整个剪辑。 如果某个部分过得太快或有些内容不清楚，唯一的选择就是倒回、浏览评论或在其他地方查找该主题。

在某个时候，我在手机上观看视频时注意到了由 Google Gemini 提供支持的“询问”按钮。 我一开始忽略了它，假设它只生成了视频的一般摘要。

但最终尝试之后，我发现这并不是我所期望的。 我可以在视频播放时提出有关视频的问题，而不是被动地在手机上观看。

Gemini 总结了视频的内容，解释了令人困惑的部分，或者提取了关键要点，而无需在应用程序之间跳转。

这就是它如何彻底改变了我的观看体验。

如何访问“提问”功能

按一个按钮并提出您的问题

您可以在 YouTube 移动应用（Android 或 iPhone）或桌面版 YouTube 网站上观看视频时访问“提问”功能。

如果可用，“询问”按钮位于视频播放器下方，通常位于“共享”和“下载”按钮之间。 点击它会打开一个聊天面板，您可以在其中输入有关视频的问题或选择建议的提示，例如总结视频。

如果您在视频下方没有看到“询问”按钮，请单击视频控件旁边的三点菜单图标。

询问功能可供美国、加拿大、新西兰、日本、印度等国家/地区的用户使用，并计划扩展到其他国家/地区。

由于推出正在进行中，一些用户可能会看到“询问”按钮，而其他用户则看不到，即使他们使用相同的设备或应用程序版本也是如此。 随着该功能变得更加稳定，谷歌预计将扩大访问范围。

当我意识到 YouTube 中可以使用“提问”功能时，我在观看视频时尝试了它。 没过多久，我们就注意到它在一些情况下变得真正有用​​。

当我忘记视频时及时补上

是时候让快退按钮休息一下了

当我不知道视频中发生了什么时，“询问”功能会很有帮助。 这种情况发生的频率比我愿意承认的要高，尤其是在观看较长的视频或同时处理多项任务时。

恢复的唯一方法是倒带视频并找出事情开始有意义的地方。 如果解释很长或者创建者快速地讨论了几个要点，这可能会令人沮丧。

使用 YouTube 上的“提问”按钮会改变这种情况。 我可以问“这一部分的要点是什么？”，而不是浏览时间线。

Gemini 提供了带有时间戳的视频内容摘要，使我能够保持专注，而无需重新观看整个内容。

决定长视频是否值得观看

一个简短的总结让我了解了故事的要点

“询问”功能的另一种有用的情况是当我决定一个长视频是否值得我花时间时。

YouTube 上充斥着时长为 15、20 或 40 分钟的视频，从标题或缩略图中并不总是能明显看出内容是否有帮助。

通常，我会跳过视频的部分内容或阅读说明以大致了解其内容。 但这并不总能给出清晰的画面。

使用 YouTube 上的“提问”按钮可以让这件事变得更容易。 在我决定观看整个视频之前，我可以要求它总结视频或突出显示要点。

如果摘要听起来很有趣，我会继续关注。 如果没有，我可以继续做其他事情，而不必花几分钟自己尝试解决这个问题。

将教程转变为分步说明

简单的步骤让学习新主题变得更容易

许多 YouTube 教程都会连续执行几个步骤，如果创作者动作太快，很容易错过一些重要的内容。

我会反复暂停视频或倒带以仔细检查下一步是什么。 这是可行的，但它可以将一个简单的教程变成在时间轴上进行大量的来回擦洗。

使用“询问”按钮，我可以请求 Google Gemini 将说明简化为清晰的步骤。

例如，我可能会要求它“列出该视频中显示的步骤”或“将本教程变成分步说明”。 Gemini 将这个过程总结为一个更容易遵循的简单列表。

复制说明并将其粘贴到文档中以便稍后保存或参考。

找到视频中重要的部分

我喜欢跳到好的部分

YouTube 最令人沮丧的事情之一就是在视频中进行搜索。

即使创作者添加了章节，您要寻找的确切时刻也并不总是显而易见的。 双子座有助于更快地缩小范围。

我可以问这样的问题：“创作者什么时候谈论电池寿命？” 或“他们在哪里解释相机设置？”

Gemini 向我指出视频的相关部分，让我更容易跳转到我想要的信息。

以更具互动性的方式观看 YouTube

使用 YouTube 的“询问”按钮几次后，我发现它在与视频一起使用时比作为简单的摘要工具更有用。

提出问题、澄清令人困惑的部分或快速理解要点可以使观看视频更具互动性。

大多数时候我仍然以同样的方式观看 YouTube，尤其是当我欣赏创作者的故事讲述或纯粹为了娱乐而观看某些内容时。

然而，当我尝试学习某些东西、遵循教程或理解长视频时，“提问”功能已成为我现在经常依赖的功能。
